discovery: Controlled/living radical polymerization (atom transfer radical polymerization), which makes it possible to synthesize polymers with precisely defined architectures
rationale: Recent Chemistry prizes went to biochemistry (2024, protein design) and to framework materials (2025, MOFs). That pattern makes a synthetic or materials chemistry prize plausible for 2026. Metal-catalyzed controlled radical polymerization, found independently by Matyjaszewski and Sawamoto in 1995, changed polymer and materials science. It has been cited very heavily, has been used across industry, and has won major awards such as the Wolf Prize. These are the hallmarks of a long-overdue Nobel topic.
